issue.title: Remove x-axis labels from the Studio revenue chart
issue.description:
Further simplify the Studio revenue composition by removing the x-axis labels from its primary Revenue chart across all range selections.

Background:
<issue id="6644c25f-7710-478c-96d6-64069a76ce49" href="https://linear.app/emman-systems/issue/PUI-85/simplify-the-studio-revenue-composition">PUI-85</issue> simplified Studio revenue by removing the title/subtitle, nested metric cards, legend, and secondary Costs series. This follow-up continues that visual simplification.

Owner direction:

* Remove the x-axis/category labels shown below the chart.
* Apply the change consistently across Week, Month, and Quarter views.
* Keep the range tabs functional and keep the primary Revenue visualization itself.

Remove:

* Week view day labels such as Mon / Tue / Wed / Thu / Fri / Sat / Sun
* Month-view x-axis/date labels
* Quarter-view x-axis/period labels
* any equivalent visible x-axis label row used by this composition

Keep:

* Week / Month / Quarter tabs
* primary Revenue line/area visualization
* current chart data behavior when switching ranges
* existing grid/reference lines if they remain part of the accepted visual treatment
* token-driven chart styling
* responsive behavior
* light/dark theme behavior

Intent:
The chart should read as a cleaner visual trend surface rather than a fully annotated analytics chart.

Do not:

* remove the primary Revenue series;
* reintroduce the Costs series or legend;
* change the range-tab behavior;
* change shared chart primitives globally unless a local composition-level configuration cannot achieve the result;
* alter other gallery charts;
* change gallery ordering or layout.

Acceptance:

* Week view shows no x-axis/day labels.
* Month view shows no x-axis/date labels.
* Quarter view shows no x-axis/period labels.
* Range tabs continue to change the chart data correctly.
* Primary Revenue line/area remains visible and responsive.
* No stale empty axis space remains after label removal.
* Light/dark/theme-token responsiveness remains intact.
* No keyboard, focus, containment, or accessibility regression.
